claims.statement: The FMC's 2024 rule gives billed parties at least 30 days to request mitigation, refund or waiver and requires carriers to provide a dispute process; a Polish exporter or importer on a US trade lane can therefore contractually mandate an agent to audit invoices and submit evidence-bound requests, subject to counsel confirming agency and jurisdiction.

Detention and demurrage are discrete invoices triggered by late container pickup or equipment return; FMC fact-finding recorded importer and exporter concern about excessive charges, and a non-compliant invoice can eliminate the billed party's obligation to pay, creating an auditable recovery event.

The payer is the shipper's CFO or logistics director from the avoided or refunded invoice, with an invoice receipt starting the 30-day action window as purchase trigger; the rule expressly identifies contracted transport customers and consignees as billable parties and makes compliant charges payable.

contrary_evidence: The cited FMC rights govern US-regulated ocean transport, so many Polish/EU port charges and forwarder pass-through invoices may fall outside the rule.
Carriers can issue fully compliant invoices for legitimate delays, leaving no recovery pool.

economics.acquisition_route: Partner with Polish customs brokers and freight forwarders serving US routes; obtain read-only invoice and shipment-timestamp access plus a narrowly drafted dispute mandate from each shipper.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Prove recovery on 100 invoices, then distribute through 20 freight partners to audit PLN 100m of annual charges; a 20% success fee on 8% recoveries would yield PLN 1.6m revenue, with expansion across Central Europe and carrier-specific rule data supporting PLN 5m founder net worth in roughly 5-7 years if recovery rates persist.
economics.founder_time: Initially 2-3 hours daily for data ingestion, exception scoring and partner management; licensed maritime counsel reviews templates and only escalated cases receive human attention.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Automated invoice checks are low marginal cost, but counsel and evidence gathering are variable; preliminary gross-margin target is 50-65% of success fees.
economics.payback: No recovery, no fee; channel acquisition should repay from the first two successful disputes per broker, and the client sees immediate positive payback because fees come from recovered cash.
economics.pricing: 15-25% of waived or refunded charges, with an optional PLN 1,000-3,000 monthly monitoring minimum for high-volume shippers.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every container movement can generate a new invoice; recurring audits, carrier rule libraries and timestamp evidence make the service habitual for active shippers.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A carrier-, terminal- and lane-specific corpus of invoice defects, event timestamps and dispute outcomes raises recovery precision and channel trust.
fingerprint.customer: Polish and Central European manufacturers, importers and exporters moving containers on FMC-regulated US trade lanes.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Revenue-share referrals embedded in customs brokers, freight forwarders and trade-finance accountants.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Continuous invoice audit and evidence-pack generation paid as a share of waived or recovered detention and demurrage charges.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The shipper's finance or logistics budget pays only when a carrier waives, credits or refunds a disputed fee.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Receipt of a detention or demurrage invoice starts a short dispute deadline.

founder_fit: The work is document-, rule- and timestamp-heavy, suiting data extraction and anomaly-detection skills.
A contingency model is cheap to validate alongside employment and avoids high-energy direct selling through broker channels.
The service can become a repeatable rules engine and proprietary outcomes dataset rather than a manual consultancy.
risks: Unauthorized-practice, agency, debt-collection or litigation rules may limit what a non-law firm may do.
Forwarders may lack complete timestamps or have contract clauses that pass through valid fees.
Carriers can improve invoices or automate defenses, compressing recovery rates.

structure.control_point: Time-limited shipper mandate plus access to invoices, contracts and container event timestamps
structure.critical_dependency: FMC applicability and complete evidence for each billed movement

thesis: Acquire a narrow dispute mandate and shipment evidence feed from European shippers on US lanes, detect detention and demurrage invoices that violate FMC requirements or fail the incentive principle, and take a percentage only when the charge is waived or refunded.
title: Container Fee Recovery Mandate
uncertainties: The addressable volume of FMC-governed invoices among Polish shippers is unknown.
Actual recovery rates and average invoice values have not been measured in this channel.
Counsel must determine which dispute actions require legal representation.
